A pitch deck is a concise and visually engaging presentation that is typically used in business settings to convey a company's or project's key information, value proposition, and investment opportunity. Pitch decks are primarily used when seeking investments, partnerships, or to secure new clients. They serve as a persuasive tool to convey the essence of your business or idea quickly and effectively. A well-crafted pitch deck can make a significant difference in the success of a business, startup, or project.

Here are the key components and the needs of usage for a pitch deck in a business context:

  1. Introduction: Start with a compelling introduction that grabs the audience's attention and provides an overview of your business or project.

  2. Problem Statement: Clearly define the problem or need that your product or service addresses. This sets the stage for why your business is relevant.

  3. Solution: Present your solution and how it addresses the identified problem. Explain how your product or service works and what makes it unique.

  4. Market Opportunity: Describe the market size and potential for your business. This includes the target audience and its demographics.

  5. Business Model: Explain how your business will generate revenue, your pricing strategy, and the sales channels you plan to use.

  6. Traction: Showcase any significant achievements, customer testimonials, or partnerships to build credibility.

  7. Competitive Analysis: Identify your competitors and explain how your business is positioned relative to them. Highlight your competitive advantages.

  8. Team: Introduce your team and their relevant experience. This builds trust and confidence in your ability to execute the business plan.

  9. Financial Projections: Present your financial forecasts, including revenue, expenses, and profitability projections. This demonstrates the potential for a return on investment.

  10. Ask: Clearly state what you are seeking from your audience, whether it's investment, partnership, or something else.


The skills related to pitching, business presenting, and business communication are important for experts and companies for several reasons:

  1. Securing Funding: Effective pitching skills are crucial when seeking investments or funding. A well-presented pitch deck can significantly increase the chances of attracting investors.

  2. Building Credibility: Strong presentation skills can help a company or individual build credibility with clients, partners, and stakeholders. A professional presentation conveys competence and confidence.

  3. Effective Communication: Business communication skills are essential for conveying ideas, plans, and strategies within a company. Clear and persuasive communication can drive team alignment and enhance productivity.

  4. Client Acquisition: In sales and client-facing roles, effective presentation and communication skills can help in acquiring new clients or customers. It can make the difference between a successful pitch and a missed opportunity.

  5. Career Advancement: For individuals, mastering these skills can lead to career advancement. Professionals who can effectively communicate their ideas and lead presentations tend to stand out and progress in their careers.

  6. Team Collaboration: Effective communication and presentation skills are essential for collaboration within teams. They help in conveying objectives, sharing updates, and ensuring everyone is on the same page.


Strong understanding of pitching, business presenting skills, and business communication skills is crucial in today's competitive business environment. These skills not only enable companies to attract investments, win clients, and build credibility but also support the career growth of individuals. A combination of these skills can lead to more successful and impactful business endeavors.

Many parents describe the desires for their children as "I want my kids to be happy" or "I want them to have a good life." But these goals are abstract and difficult to achieve once, let alone repeat.


SMART Goals Parenting breaks these (and other) abstract desires down into their basic foundational components that allow you and your child to achieve happiness, connection, trust and respect... repeatedly.


SMART Goals Parenting's objective is to provide you with the knowledge and tools to cultivate your desired relationship with your child while also preparing your child for being able to one day cultivate happiness and success for him/herself.

You will learn the two SMART goals, which will be your guiding lights are you traverse the terrain of parenthood.


As long as you maintain your focus on what you are ultimately trying to achieve you won't get lost in the minutia.

After learning the SMART goals you will learn how to identify and avoid the pitfalls of choosing fear over love and discarding self-care.


Engaging in these two behaviors will sabotage all of your work. It will be like pouring water into a bottle with no bottom. If you have ever felt unappreciated, unloved, disrespected or criticized for your parenting efforts then I am certain one or both of these barriers are at play.

The next few lessons will tackle guidance.


My goal is to get you to the point when guiding your child is a simple conversation in which both of you feel understood and respected. Until then, you may need these skills to help you navigate.


Choices, Consequences, Rewards and Reinforce (CCRR) are the four parts of seamless discipline.


Streamline how you discipline and remove all power struggles. Doing so will solidify you as your child's respected figure and someone s/he can look up to.


The last, but not least topics covered are the most used parts of communication - listening and speaking. You should listen to understand and speak to build trust.


Many Parents, Myself included have practiced these, eliminating Parenting Stress, following Structured Guidance, helping to Raise Healthy, Confident and Motivated Children.


I look forward to helping you do the same.


Best regards,

Helen V Hicks MA MBA LPC

Licensed Professional Counselor, Parenting Coach

Tu as l’impression de travailler beaucoup sans vraiment avancer sur les projets qui comptent ?

Entre les notifications, les messages, les obligations quotidiennes et les interruptions permanentes, il devient difficile de disposer de plusieurs heures consécutives pour réfléchir, créer et travailler en profondeur.

La Retraite Ermite propose une approche radicalement simple : t’isoler volontairement pendant 48 heures pour réduire au maximum les distractions et consacrer un week-end entier à un projet important.

48 heures pour retrouver ta concentration

Depuis 2018, j’organise régulièrement mes propres week-ends ermites dans différentes villes du monde, notamment à Wellington, Auckland, Adélaïde, Sydney et Melbourne.

L’idée est simple : préparer à l’avance un environnement dans lequel tu peux fonctionner de manière aussi autonome que possible pendant 48 heures afin de consacrer ton attention à un objectif précis.

J’ai testé différentes durées et différentes façons de procéder. Certaines expériences ont très bien fonctionné, d’autres beaucoup moins : une semaine entière d’ermite à Auckland s’est notamment révélée catastrophique.

Ces expériences m’ont progressivement permis d’affiner une méthode plus simple, réaliste et reproductible.

Prépare ta propre Retraite Ermite

Dans ce cours, tu vas apprendre à organiser ton premier week-end ermite de A à Z.

Tu verras notamment comment :

  • choisir un objectif clair pour tes 48 heures ;

  • sélectionner un environnement adapté ;

  • préparer ce dont tu auras besoin avant de commencer ;

  • réduire les interruptions et les distractions ;

  • désactiver tes principaux « tueurs de productivité » ;

  • organiser tes périodes de travail et de récupération ;

  • créer les conditions favorables à un travail plus profond ;

  • faire le bilan de l’expérience et améliorer ta prochaine retraite.

L’objectif n’est pas de travailler frénétiquement pendant 48 heures ni de supprimer le sommeil et les pauses. Il s’agit au contraire de protéger ton attention suffisamment longtemps pour avancer sur un travail qui reste habituellement fragmenté par le quotidien.

Découvre également le principe de la Think Week

Nous explorerons aussi le concept de Think Week, notamment popularisé par Bill Gates lorsqu’il dirigeait Microsoft : une période volontairement consacrée à la lecture, à la réflexion et à la prise de recul.

Tu verras comment t’inspirer de cette idée sans nécessairement reproduire son organisation, afin de créer une version adaptée à ta situation, ton travail et tes objectifs.

Une retraite peut ainsi servir non seulement à produire, mais également à penser, écrire, lire, prendre des décisions importantes ou retrouver une direction plus claire.

Ce cours s’adresse particulièrement aux entrepreneurs, créateurs, freelances, indépendants et professionnels qui ont un projet important sur lequel ils aimeraient avancer avec moins d’interruptions.

Il peut notamment t’être utile si tu as un projet que tu repousses depuis longtemps, si tes journées sont constamment fragmentées ou si tu souhaites expérimenter une méthode concrète pour créer une période de concentration profonde.

Tu n’as pas besoin de partir à l’autre bout du monde ni de disparaître pendant une semaine. Commence simplement avec un projet, un environnement adapté et 48 heures que tu décides de protéger.

Ton prochain week-end ermite commence ici.

Le cours ne garantit pas qu’un travail nécessitant normalement plusieurs semaines pourra être terminé en 48 heures. · MA (moving-average model)

· ARMA (autoregressive-moving-average model)

· ARIMA (autoregressive integrated moving average model)

. SARIA (seasonal autoregressive moving average model)

. SARIMA (seasonal autoregressive integrated moving average model)

. SARIMAX (seasonal autoregressive integrated moving average model with exogenous variables)

· ARCH (autoregressive conditional heteroscedasticity model)

Gratitude, the attitude that sometimes seem counter-intuitive, especially when we look around and find no reason to engage in it.

It is defined as the quality of being thankful; readiness to show appreciation for and to return kindness.

Beyond that, it is a quality or trait that you can express by reflection, self and for the people, things and circumstances around you.

It has a few powerful side effects. Some include:

- A change in perspective

- Uplifting ones mood

- Creating a suitable environment, at least within ones mind, that facilitates good decision making   


Gratitude for what, many ask?

Gratitude for Health, Sleep, Food, Body, Mind, Wellbeing, Peace of Mind, Finances, a job, career, income, roof over ones head, ability to earn, appreciate the way the world works and make a living out of it.

Gratitude for interactions, relationships with those around us, our families, children, parents, friends, colleagues, associates.

Gratitude for our professional situations, abilities, opportunities, overcoming challenges and much more.


To build this perspective into ones life is a gift one should bestow on ones self. It helps open up new perspectives at all times.

It also has immense benefits for your health - mentally, physically, emotionally. IT helps with better sleep, better self esteem, improved moods and much more.


The opportunities we have in this one life will be amplified and optimised by a quality such as Gratitude in our lives.


Gratitude to people also help forge better relations. It does not mean we should cease to have our own minds or always defer to what the people we are grateful to want, but it should be demonstrated genuinely, from the heart at every deserving opportunity. It is a privilege to have others support, care and help us.

We ourselves would do well to seek out people to support, care for and help. Not in search of gratitude or having them in our debt, but to show how grateful we are for the things that have come our way, without expecting anything from anyone in return.


Lastly, Gratitude to who?


Whoever you decide or However or Whatever you decide to show Gratitude to in your own way.

One God. One fundamental religion. Many prophets. Different Sharia. One continuing message.

courseDetails.longDescription:

17 Common Misconceptions About Islam

What do Muslims really believe—and how much of what we hear about Islam comes from reliable information rather than stereotypes, dramatic headlines, cultural practices, or individual behaviour?

17 Common Misconceptions About Islam is a clear, friendly, and beginner-level course designed to help non-Muslims and curious learners understand Islam more accurately. No previous knowledge of Islam, Arabic, or religious studies is required.

Throughout the course, we examine 17 widely repeated misconceptions and replace confusion with clear, balanced explanations. You will explore questions such as:

  • Is Allah a different God?

  • Do Muslims worship Prophet Muhammad?

  • What does Islam teach about Jesus and Mary?

  • Is the Quran simply a copy of the Bible?

  • Are all Muslims Arabs—and are all Arabs Muslims?

  • Does Islam deny women rights, education, or employment?

  • Can Muslim men marry an unlimited number of women?

  • Do Muslims worship the Kaaba?

  • Does Islam reject happiness, science, education, or modern technology?

  • Is Sharia only concerned with harsh punishments?

The course also teaches an essential critical-thinking skill: how to distinguish religious teachings, cultural traditions, political decisions, and personal behaviour. This helps learners avoid judging an entire religion through the actions of one person, one government, or one cultural community.

Each lesson uses simple language, relatable examples, and gentle humour to make complex subjects easier to understand. The purpose is not to pressure learners to accept a religion or to avoid genuine differences between faiths. Instead, the course encourages respectful curiosity, accurate understanding, and informed discussion.

By the end, you will have a stronger foundation for evaluating claims about Islam, checking sources and context, communicating respectfully with Muslims, and separating verified teachings from misinformation.

Bring your curiosity, your questions, and an open mind. No Arabic examination is waiting for you—and you will not be asked to memorize the Quran before lunch.
